title: Fats Navarro and playing what is happening
summary: Clifford Brown came out of Navarro; Mingus compares playing the moment to ballads.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Fats Navarro is obviously a figure in your book. My sense of it is that in terms of the histories these days, people tend to either ignore him or underestimate him. How important --
Yeah. You'll see his name, but he doesn't get the space that he should get. How important was he?
Well, it's hard to tell, man, it's hard to say what a guy is giving. Like, Clifford Brown came out of Fats Navarro (unintelligible).

More than he did out of Dizzy. Fats was warm in his playing. (And he had all the tricks, he had all the embellishments, he had -- I remember, he told a story. See, when Bird and them was coming up, they were talking to
each other, telling stories about their lives, about what they'd been doing.
I remember Fats Dinefo playing (singing), and then he played Pretty Baby.
And I looked out and there was a girl with a blue dress on, in the audience. He was playing the now, whether you wanted to listen to it or not. Charlie Parker did the same thing.
And that's what you always do, isn't it?

Yeah, when I was playing, I tried to talk about what was going around. Except on the ballad. When I play the ballad, I play all the pain I've in my life. Man, I got to get this chair straight. Can you cut that off for a minute?
Hey, Sue, can you cut this off a minute? Where's ?
